approach: issue #60: schema/v1.json is a fork of the upstream Agent Plugins Specification v1.0.0 manifest schema. Split it on the ownership line -- the manifest envelope is upstream's (delete the fork, point at the published schema URL the manifests already declare), the extensions['org.cyberuni.universal-plugin'] namespace body is ours (retain, scoped to the namespace object as its root, re-stating nothing of the spec around it).

SCOPE SPLIT: the schema file and the two skills/init documents that hand out the raw-branch URL are non-behavioral -- no code loads them, no observable CLI behavior moves -- so they are carried in this CR and ESCAPE the suite (no spec node, no scenarios). The behavioral half is one unit, plugin/build/: readSkills resolved only the string form of a pathValue, so the array and { paths } forms silently fell back to ./skills/. That is a contract the retained schema states and the build does not honor.

ADDITIVE on the frozen plugin/build/build.feature -- 8 new scenarios, gherkin-cli diff and classify-edit-class both report ADDITIVE / addOnly true (8 added, 0 modified, 0 removed), so the freeze self-clears and no re-open ratification is needed. Root spec.md stays status: implemented -- an additive scenario does not unfreeze, so there is no implemented->draft revert. No Clearance floor.

PLACEMENT: the retained schema ships inside the npm package (packages/universal-plugin/schema/, added to files) rather than at the repo root, because the issue's own motivation is a consumer resolving these fields against an installed dependency. It carries NO $id -- the old one advertised a raw.githubusercontent branch URL and the repo publishes no schema host, so asserting a URL nothing serves would repeat the defect in a new place.

IN SCOPE beyond the issue's letter: extracting the namespace subtree and validating it for the first time exposed that the four harnessExtension* blocks were additionalProperties:false while the build copies each block VERBATIM -- the repo's own examples/research-workbench manifest fails the old schema on harnesses.claude-code.governances and .assets. Opened those four blocks with a $comment stating why. A contract that rejects the repo's own working example is not a contract.

auto-all: the change is additive at the suite, the non-behavioral half is a delete-plus-scoped-retain of an artifact no code reads, and the code fix is covered by 8 tests proven to bite (a cold judge independently reverted the resolver and confirmed 5 of the 8 fail). Self-assert both gates within leash after the cold judges pass; Clearance/Compatibility/Conflict floors still stop.

what: plugin/build/ and plugin/bundle/ node specs are missing the mandatory behavioral sections: ## What, ## Control Flow (a drawn CFG), and a ## Scenario map with the 1:1 | Edge | Path (Given) | Scenario | binding. Both carry ## Use Cases plus an untitled behavior/coverage table that stands in for the map. Six sibling nodes (plugin/version, plugin/install, plugin/init, marketplace/init, marketplace/validate) already carry the full structure, so the two are the outliers. Because neither node declares a ## Scenario map, check-suite skips its map-binding lint entirely -- the scenario<->edge coverage of the largest suite in the corpus is unlinted.
why-not-now: pre-existing on both nodes and unrelated to this CR's subject (schema ownership). Bringing build/ into conformance means drawing a CFG over 44 existing scenarios and writing a 44-row map -- a formation-scale change to a contract this CR does not otherwise touch, and it would land unreviewed alongside a schema split. This CR followed the node's existing convention rather than half-converting it.

what: The retained extension schema is not loaded by any code. plugin validate is specced but impl-deferred, so the field set it now states machine-readably is still enforced only by TypeScript types and by hand. Wiring plugin validate to check extensions['org.cyberuni.universal-plugin'] against schema/extension.schema.json is what turns the retained half from documentation into a contract.
why-not-now: issue #60 is scoped to the ownership split, and explicitly records plugin validate as impl-deferred. Building the verb is its own CR against the plugin/validate node.

why: Component path resolution on plugin/build/: the extension's pathValue contract (a './' path string, an array of them, or a { paths } object) is now stated in the node README and covered by 8 ADDITIVE scenarios on the frozen build.feature -- readSkills had honored only the string form, so the array and { paths } forms fell back to ./skills/ in silence. Cold sdd-spec-judge 3-lens {oracle,builder,architect} all PASS, ALIGNED true. The judge re-ran the miss test independently by reverting the resolver: 5 of the 8 fail against the old code, confirming discrimination; the 3 that pass are the positive companions the Builder bar requires. Rounds 1-3 were BLOCKED at the governance pre-flight (producer had authored against project content without loading the bar bodies); remediated by loading all seven, which surfaced a real coverage hole -- a warning branch for a malformed declaration with no scenario -- closed as the 8th scenario. check-spec-state OK, check-suite OK, classify-edit-class ADDITIVE (8 added / 0 modified / 0 removed), check-spec-structure and check-scenario-overlap 0 blocking, 0 open markers. Freeze self-clears (additive), so root status stays implemented and no re-open was needed. CONFORMANCE warn: plugin/build/README.md lacks ## What / ## Control Flow / ## Scenario map -- pre-existing, shared with plugin/bundle/, judged a legitimate deferral and recorded as a followup.

Cold sdd-impl-judge (ADR-0016; each of the 8 frozen scenarios' oracle re-derived from the .feature before reading the tests) -> IMPLEMENTATION_PASS true, 8/8 passing. The judge did not take the green run on trust: it re-ran the mutation experiment itself, reverting readSkills to the pre-CR string-only resolver and confirming 5 of the 8 fail, with the 3 survivors being exactly the positive companions the Builder bar requires, then restored the tree byte-identical. It also enumerated resolvePathValue's real branches beyond the suite -- skills: null and an array carrying a non-string are both correctly rejected fail-loud; skills: [] and { paths: [] } return empty in silence, but both are schema-invalid (minItems 1) and inert, recorded as a followup rather than a blocker. Full package verification green at 594 tests (was 586); knip findings in src/install and src/run confirmed byte-identical to origin/main, so pre-existing. No absorption finding: no scenario apparatus (my-skills, a-skills, alpha, beta, missing, ignored, the literal 7) appears in the implementation. Judged on the tree rebased onto origin/main 7a1d660, which is what will land. No frozen .feature edited.

what: resolvePathValue returns an empty path list without warning for skills: [] and skills: { paths: [] }, which diverges from the rule the sibling branches follow -- a declaration the resolver cannot use warns rather than reading nothing in silence. Both shapes are already schema-invalid (extension.schema.json gives pathValue's array form and pathConfig.paths minItems 1), so a schema-conformant manifest cannot reach the state, and the failure mode is inert: fewer skills derived, never wrong ones. Extending the warn-on-unusable-declaration rule to schema-invalid-but-parseable shapes wants its own scenario.
why-not-now: no frozen scenario names it, the state is unreachable through a valid manifest, and adding a warning for it would widen this CR's contract past what the issue asked for. Surfaced by the cold impl-judge's branch enumeration, not by a failing scenario.
